intro: Tesla Trader Link arrives with the familiar pitch: AI analysis, automatic entries, a US$250 start and a practice account. The pitch is polished. The fine print is where the questions begin, and that is what this review measures.
The desk runs in the browser. Models produce signals across 10 assets, the broker partner holds funds, and the platform charges no fee of its own - spreads and overnight charges still apply.
Our method is a desk review: no funded account, no trades. We read the published material in full, including unfilled placeholders and contradictions, and scored five fixed dimensions.
whatItClaims: Withdrawals processed in under a day, per the page.
No prior trading experience required.
AI and algorithmic market analysis producing signals and suggested entries.
Automatic or manual execution, with a browser-based platform.
No platform fees - broker spreads and overnight charges still apply.
whatWeChecked: The template marks: unfilled placeholders left in the wording.
The performance story: no verified track record behind the return claims.
The number reuse: one score figure doing more than one job.
The deposit terms: minimum amount, payment methods and where the money sits.
The demo claim: practice account confirmed in the signup flow.
The payout promise: within-a-day wording without processing detail.

Free registration and a demo account.
cons: The headline fee claim and the real cost disagree.
Two conflicting support figures.
Restriction lists disagree.
Unfilled template placeholders.
redFlags: Support figures that contradict each other.
Template placeholders left unrendered.
Return claims without verification.

faqs.q: Can I trade manually?
faqs.a: Yes - the platform offers automatic and manual modes, so you can follow the signals or confirm each entry yourself.

faqs.q: Is Tesla Trader Link safe, legit or a scam?
faqs.a: We found no scam indicators in the product, which reads as a functioning AI trading service. The conditions are editorial: claims without verification, conflicting figures and restriction lists that disagree. We rate it safe to research with the conditions in this review.

faqs.q: Does it offer a demo account?
faqs.a: Yes - a practice account is part of the package and runs alongside the live balance, which is the sensible first step before risking the US$250 minimum.

faqs.q: What does the published score actually mean?
faqs.a: It does double duty - a platform score and an early community response - and neither is independently verified. Treat both as marketing until proven otherwise.

faqs.q: How much support does it offer?
faqs.a: Unclear - around-the-clock coverage is claimed, while other sections quote different figures. Ask support to reconcile them before you fund anything.

bottomLine: What we found is a real service wrapped in marketing that outruns its own fine print. Trade the service, not the marketing.
We rate it 4.5 with conditions: the platform is usable, the published claims are not all verifiable, and the US$250 minimum is the right size for testing either.
